A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Con2 research despite the changed title. All 20 pages of v2 and 27 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, figures, and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original medical and natural-image anomaly-detection experiments in Section 4 and Appendix E, including a multiple-context ablation.

after.justification: v3 reports original experiments on six medical datasets, retained natural-image benchmarks, and new loss-component, runtime, clustering, and backbone analyses.

M1.justification: The shared encoder, two projection heads, weighted context-contrasting and content-alignment losses, and SNND/SLH scoring procedures remain. Rewritten equations and newly disclosed architecture details do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: v3 adds BreastMNIST ultrasound, OctMNIST retinal OCT, Kvasir endoscopy, and BR35H brain MRI evaluations. Pneumonia, Melanoma, and all five natural-image benchmarks remain, substantially broadening medical coverage.

E2.justification: The medical comparison adds AnomalyCLIP, I-JEPA-ZSAD, I-JEPA-AD, MVFA, MediCLIP, and PANDA while retaining the earlier baselines. CLIP-AD's natural-image comparison in v2 Table 3 is removed; the other natural-image comparators remain in v3's figures.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce fine-tuning and additional zero-shot configurations, ViT-Tiny versus ViT-Base controls, individual-loss controls, silhouette scoring, and runtime sweeps over training-set and batch counts. The retained Con2 recipe, including 2048 epochs, optimization settings, and dataset preprocessing, is unchanged as reported.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct tests of each loss component, quantitative context-cluster measurements, anomaly-score runtime scaling, and I-JEPA backbone sensitivity. It expands score and augmentation analyses across medical datasets and replaces the CIFAR10 PCA case with BR35H. The earlier multiple-context ablation remains in Appendix E.2.

E5.justification: The general three-seed, mean-plus-standard-deviation practice remains. However, retained medical SLH comparisons previously tabulated with standard deviations in v2 Table 1 appear as mean-only bars in v3 Figure 3, reducing uncertainty reporting for those results.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive medical and diagnostic results and revises retained scores. Melanoma Con2-Invert/SNND changes from 91.8±0.2 to 94.1±0.4; CIFAR100 Con2-Flip/SNND changes from 90.8±4.8 to 89.7±4.2. These revisions lack an accompanying reported method or setting change. Detailed per-class results in v2 Tables 4–8 are removed.

T1.justification: v3 adds an explicit distribution-symmetry relation in Equation 11 and O(nd) versus O(d²) memory/runtime reasoning in Appendix E.3. The distinctiveness and alignment conditions already existed; most other mathematical edits restate the existing formulation.

C1.justification: Con2, context augmentations, and the two anomaly scores remain the central contributions. v3 describes natural-image performance as competitive, tempering v2's concluding claim of consistent baseline superiority, while emphasizing superiority on specialized medical benchmarks.

C2.justification: v3 adds hypotheses about loss-component collapse, cluster overlap, and nonelliptical clusters limiting SLH. Melanoma flipping changes from an example of failure attributed to violated distinctiveness to successful performance despite that violation. New limitations explicitly address image-only evaluation, augmentation difficulties in other modalities, and absent theoretical guarantees.

D1.justification: v3 adds a Con2 code-access link, projection-head and encoder details, CLIP prompts, implementation instructions for new baselines, and preprocessing information for four new datasets. These are disclosures rather than established changes to the retained method. Compute reporting adds the new medical datasets but removes natural-image runtime entries.

R1.justification: v3 adds references and discussion for I-JEPA, PANDA, MVFA, MediCLIP, regularization approaches, and new datasets and analyses. It separates pretrained-model approaches from outlier exposure, which v2 grouped together, while retaining the central positioning around learning from normal data without simulating anomalies.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Contrastive learning becomes a separate methods subsection, context augmentation moves after the objective, experimental sections expand and reorganize, and the dataset and experimental-detail appendices exchange order.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the training diagram, replaces the PCA illustration and adds an OCC schematic, restructures medical tables, and adds loss, score, runtime, and clustering plots. Augmentation illustrations are reorganized between main text and appendix, while the five detailed per-class tables are removed. Typography and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of the central claims: broader medical comparisons test applicability, loss ablations test the combined objective, and clustering and timing analyses support the representation and efficiency arguments. Added implementation information and explicit limitations also improve assessability. These gains outweigh the loss of detailed natural-image tables and remaining reporting inconsistencies, such as the BreastMNIST standard-deviation mismatch between v3 Tables 1 and 2.
